Senses.Explanation: The term names the named teacher in each cited record’s recorded act of approving or certifying a person’s understanding; the entries keep that act distinct from assigning succession. Literally, "seal" (印) and "approve or permit" (可): "approve and certify," attested 761 times in 173 allowlisted texts. Lamp and lineage records use the verb for recorded acts of approval. After a student opens to understanding at Tianyi's assembly, Tianyi "approves him, saying: this is my house's thousand-mile colt" (印可曰，此吾家千里駒也). Another account says an unnamed interlocutor approved six people individually and told them, "you six people together verify my body; each accords with one part" (汝等六人，同證吾身，各契其一). Narrative forms include "all received approval" (皆蒙印可), "deeply received approval" (profoundly receiving the seal of approval), and "received the named record subject's approval" (receiving an unnamed interlocutor’s seal of approval). These passages record approval, the named record subject's words at approval, and who received it; they do not make every occurrence a single theory of what was certified.
Senses.Note: Approval is not always the end of examination. In the Zhang Shangying case, after Donglin has approved the commissioner, Doushuai asks whether he still has any doubt about the words and teachings of buddhas and ancestral teachers. Historical notices also distinguish a person's approving teacher from the lineage teacher ultimately named in succession: one person can receive approval from more than one unnamed interlocutor while a later record names a particular succession relation. The headword records the approval event; lineage assignment remains a separate structural claim.
